transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-06-07 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood CSM); Maria Gonzales (NexGen Head of Data), Ethan Riley (Infra), Priya Menon (Security)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to scope Private/VPC deployment. Focus: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink/private endpoints, region constraints, egress, KMS and audit logs.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, and we can go into your infra constraints.
[00:10] Maria: thanks Samir. yeah we run a hybrid AWS environment, mostly us-east-1 for dev and eu-west-1 for prod workloads, so region questions are huge for us.
[00:22] Jia: great, and to set expectations we're here to talk about Redwood Private — we support VPC peering and private endpoints, and there's an on-prem bundle if you need air-gapped.
[00:35] Ethan: okay quick context: currently all our ML inference runs on ECS and EKS in our prod eu-west-1 region. we have strict egress rules, outbound via a proxy and somethings go through a central NAT. latency to models matters but so does data residency.
[00:50] Priya: plus SOC2 and audit log retention requirements. we need KMS integration for customer keys and want to ensure logs go to our splunk stack.
[01:05] Samir: understood. high level options — hosted (not likely given regs), dedicated (reserved infra in our infra, isolated but still managed), and private (control plane in your VPC or private control plane with customer-managed network). for private we can either do VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (private endpoints), or a transit-gateway approach.
[01:30] Maria: what's the difference for us practically? like network rules, ports, egress?
[01:37] Jia: with VPC peering you get layer3 connectivity — simple, low latency — but peering is regional unless you set up inter-region peering or route via TGW. PrivateLink gives you an ENI-backed endpoint in your VPC and is more controlled: you don't need route table changes across all subnets, and security teams often prefer it. however PrivateLink can be more expensive at scale.
[02:05] Ethan: and peering requires us to open up certain subnets — how do we handle overlapping CIDRs? we have several teams with /16s that sometimes collide.
[02:16] Jia: overlapping CIDR is the typical blocker. if CIDR overlap exists we recommend either using a transit gateway with NAT or using PrivateLink which avoids peering. we also discussed a NAT egress pattern where Redwood sits in a private subnet with egress via customer NAT — that keeps IP egress under customer control.
[02:38] Priya: KMS — can we bring our key? HSM?
[02:42] Samir: yes we support customer-managed keys (CMK) integrated with your KMS; for on-prem we offer HSM integrations — there is an additional compliance review and SOW item. we'll send the KMS integration doc.
[02:55] Maria: about regions — you mentioned eu-west-1. can we pin to our region for all traffic? we can't have any token routing to us-east.
[03:06] Jia: you can. Redwood Private can be deployed into your eu-west-1 VPC — control plane and serving plane colocated — we can also restrict routing so requests never leave eu-west-1. for Hosted we have multi-region but that would not satisfy your data residency requirement.
[03:25] Ethan: what about latency? we need sub-100ms for simple token generations for our triage helpers.
[03:33] Jia: sub-100ms is achievable depending on model and instance type. with dedicated GPU pools colocated that are pinned to your region and tuned kernel selection we can hit that, but it depends on batching and request size. also note that enabling prefix caching (KV cache) helps — sorry i mean KV cache — reduces repeated token cost and latency for repeated contexts.
[03:56] Maria: any firewall ports we need to open? our security team doesn't like opening many ports.
[04:01] Jia: minimal outbound allowed — typically HTTPS over port 443 to our private endpoints or to the specific ENI if using PrivateLink. If peering, route table entries and security groups must allow inter-subnet traffic to serving subnets, again generally port 443. we avoid wide open SSH or database ports.
[04:22] Priya: what about audit logs? must ship to splunk with a retention of 7 years.
[04:28] Samir: we can forward audit logs to your logging endpoint — options: S3 export or direct push to Splunk via a connector. retention is on your side, we can keep a copy per contract but long-term retention usually resides in customer-managed S3 or your SIEM. we'll capture exact retention in the SOW.
[04:50] Maria: regulatory note: some of our data is PHI, we need HIPAA handling and BAAs. do you have experience with that?
[04:59] Samir: yes, Redwood has customers in healthcare. we support BAAs and have HIPAA controls in private deployments. there are additional security reviews and potentially a private on-prem package if required by audit.
[05:12] Ethan: networking detail: do you prefer peering directly to our app VPC or via a dedicated infra VPC? we have a shared services VPC for infra components.
[05:21] Jia: we typically recommend a dedicated Redwood service VPC that peers to your infra VPC or attaches via PrivateLink to your shared services VPC. that reduces cross-account routing changes and lets us manage subnets we control — but we can also deploy into your account into a customer-managed subnet if that's policy-required.
[05:40] Priya: any impact to our IP allowlists? if we do PrivateLink i guess the traffic originates from our ENI, but if peered then Redwood IPs show up across subnets...
[05:52] Jia: correct. with PrivateLink the endpoint IPs are inside your VPC and you control security groups. with peering you'd add peer route entries and allow the Redwood subnet CIDRs in security groups. for strict allowlists we do support static IP ranges for egress, but if you require absolute deterministic egress IPs we can run egress through your NAT.
[06:14] Maria: who owns TLS certs and mTLS for internal comms?
[06:18] Samir: TLS termination happens at the edge; for private deployments we support mutual TLS for service-to-service if you need it, and certs can be customer-managed. we'll put details in the runbook.
[06:31] Ethan: how about upgrades and rollouts — can we do canary within our VPC?
[06:35] Jia: yes, rollouts are supported — you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts at the route level; we can integrate it with your CI/CD or do it from the Redwood Console in your private control plane.
[06:50] Maria: what's a realistic timeline from kickoff to pilot? we have procurement windows.
[06:55] Samir: for a Private in-VPC pilot typically 4-6 weeks: network setup and security review (1-2 weeks), deployment and basic tests (1-2 weeks), benchmark and tuning (1-2 weeks). if there's CIDR overlap or complex transit gating add 1-2 weeks.
[07:15] Priya: can you run benchmarks in our account? we prefer the SE run them from our network to measure e2e latency.
[07:21] Jia: absolutely — we can run an SE-led benchmark from your env. we'll need test harness, sample prompts, and access to a test subnet or temporary credentials in a limited role. we have a benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://bit.ly/rw-bench-2027) that lists metrics we collect.
[07:39] Maria: cost question — does Private cost more than Dedicated?
[07:44] Samir: Private often has a higher setup fee but can be cost-competitive on ongoing infra if you provide the infra and manage egress. Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved infra) simplifies ops but is a predictable committed cost. We'll share a TCO worksheet.
[07:59] Ethan: do you support cross-account deployment? like Redwood deploys into our AWS account with roles?
[08:05] Jia: we support both: customer-managed account deployment (we deploy into your account with restricted roles) or Redwood-managed infra peered into your account. Both are common.
[08:18] Olivia: quick note on security reviews — we'll attach our SOC2 and pentest summary, and we can start the ATO package if needed.
[08:25] Priya: SSO — we use Okta and want SAML SSO for console access and RBAC.
[08:31] Samir: supported. we integrate with Okta SAML and map groups to roles. we'll include sample SAML metadata in the runbook.
[08:40] Maria: small thing — do you support private endpoints for the metrics/observability data to avoid public egress to hosted telemetry?
[08:48] Jia: yes we can ship metrics over PrivateLink into your observability VPC or push to a customer-managed collector inside your VPC; telemetry endpoints can be routed via your private peering.
[09:00] Ethan: got it. any blockers we should flag before we run the network workshop?
[09:05] Jia: primary blockers: CIDR overlap, egress NAT design, compliance docs timeline for KMS/HSM, and whether you want Redwood-managed infra or customer-managed account. If we get CIDRs and region decision, we can draft the network diagram.
[09:24] Maria: ok we'll dig up the CIDRs and confirm region (probably eu-west-1). Also Priya will review KMS/HSM constraints.
[09:33] Samir: excellent. i'll send the runbook and a proposed SOW and timeline. Jia will prepare a VPC peering vs PrivateLink diagram and an initial checklist.
[09:45] Olivia: i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the network design workshop.
[09:50] Maria: thanks all, this was helpful.
[09:54] Samir: recap / next steps: share runbook + KMS doc, customer to share CIDRs and security contacts, schedule workshop for next week. any final q's?
[10:05] Maria: none. thanks.

References: Security runbook: https://redwood.example.com/security-onboarding.pdf ; Benchmark sheet: https://bit.ly/rw-bench-2027 ; Draft SOW template: internal link (will be shared)

Auto-summary (end): action items captured, schedule workshop, next steps for CIDR and KMS review.
